AbstractText.Label: AIMS
AbstractText.content: This study estimates the prevalence of chlamydia infection amongst teenage substance users aged 14-18years and investigates risk factors associated with a positive diagnosis of chlamydia infection.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Data was collected from the medical files of adolescents who attended a statewide drug and alcohol treatment facility during a three-year period commencing June 2011.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: The highest rate of chlamydia detection (18.0%) was found in the group with a reported history of abuse, a non-substance use psychiatric diagnosis, and individuals who did not complete year 10 education.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Adolescents attending a detoxification facility are a suitable group for targeted chlamydia infection screening and early treatment.
